Premise correction: there is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware in this repository — none exists, so it cannot be located or have request limits reported.

What actually exists at the equivalent registration point is the Connect RPC interceptor chain, wired up in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (lines 134-137):

```134:137:server/router/api/v1/v1.go
		NewMetadataInterceptor(), // Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata first
		NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
		NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
		NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
```

These interceptors, defined in `server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`, only handle: header→metadata conversion, request logging, panic recovery, and authentication/authorization. None of them count, throttle, or reject requests based on rate.

Supporting evidence that no rate limiting exists anywhere in the codebase:
- A repo-wide search for `rate.limit|ratelimit|throttle|limiter` (case-insensitive, across `.go` files) turns up only one hit: a comment in `internal/email/doc.go` line 86 suggesting rate-limiting email sending as a *future* improvement — it's not implemented.
- The only other file named `*middleware*` is `internal/scheduler/middleware.go`, which provides `Recovery`, `Logging`, and `Timeout` middleware for background job handlers (not HTTP/API requests), again with no rate-limiting logic.
- `go.mod`/`go.sum` contain no rate-limiting library (e.g. `golang.org/x/time/rate`, `ulule/limiter`, `didip/tollbooth`, `throttled`).

So there's no per-user API rate-limiting middleware to cite limits for.
